questions.stem: Which form of energy does a rolling football have?

explain.why: A football does not give out light.
No electric current flows through a football.
Potential energy is stored energy, for example in an object that is high up. A rolling ball is moving.

solution: Any moving object has kinetic energy.

questions.stem: A book rests on a high shelf. Which form of energy does it have because of its height?

explain.why: The book is not making any sound.
Being high up does not make the book hot.
Kinetic energy is the energy of movement. The book is not moving.

solution: An object that is high up can fall, so it has gravitational potential energy.

questions.stem: Which of the following gives out light energy?

explain.why: A ringing bell gives out sound energy.
It has potential energy stored in it. It does not shine.
A rolling marble has kinetic energy. It does not give out light.

solution: A flame gives out light energy, and heat energy too.

questions.stem: Which of these things gives out sound energy?
options: A book lying on a desk
A torch that is switched off
A drum that is being hit
A pencil in a pencil case

explain.why: It is not moving or vibrating, so it makes no sound.
A torch gives out light, not sound, and this one is off.
A pencil that is not moving gives out no sound.

solution: A drum skin shakes when it is hit and gives out sound energy.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT a form of energy?

explain.why: Light is a form of energy. We see with it.
Heat is a form of energy. It makes things warm.
Sound is a form of energy. We hear it.

solution: Friction is a force that acts when two surfaces rub. It is not a form of energy.

questions.stem: A hairdryer is plugged into a socket and switched on. Which form of energy does the hairdryer take in?

explain.why: Heat energy is given out by the hairdryer. It does not come from the socket.
The noise it makes is given out, not taken in.
The fan inside moves, so kinetic energy is given out, not taken in.

solution: A socket supplies electrical energy. The hairdryer changes it into heat, kinetic and sound energy.

questions.stem: A ceiling fan is switched on. Which energy conversion takes place?

explain.why: The blades do not store energy. They move.
The fan does not take in light energy.
The fan uses electricity to move. It does not make electricity.

solution: The motor changes electrical energy into the kinetic energy of the turning blades.

questions.stem: A torch is switched on. Which energy conversion mainly takes place in the bulb?

explain.why: Nothing in the bulb moves.
A torch bulb does not make a sound.
That is what a solar panel does. A torch bulb gives out light.

solution: The bulb changes electrical energy into light energy (and a little heat).

questions.stem: A solar panel is placed in bright sunshine. Which energy conversion takes place?

explain.why: A solar panel does not use sound.
A solar panel itself does not move.
A solar panel makes electricity. It does not make light.

solution: A solar panel changes light energy from the Sun into electrical energy.

questions.stem: Sam rubs his hands together quickly and they become warm. Which energy conversion takes place?

explain.why: His moving hands make the heat. The heat does not make the hands move.
His hands are not storing energy, and no loud sound is made.
His hands do not shine.

solution: Rubbing is movement against friction, so kinetic energy changes into heat energy.

questions.stem: A toaster toasts a slice of bread. Which energy conversion mainly takes place in the toaster?

explain.why: A toaster does not mainly make sound.
The toaster uses electricity to make heat, not the other way round.
A toaster is not powered by light.

solution: The wires in the toaster become hot when electricity flows, so electrical energy changes to heat energy.

questions.stem: A loudspeaker plays music. Which energy conversion takes place?

explain.why: That is what a microphone does. A loudspeaker gives out sound.
A loudspeaker is not made to shine.
A loudspeaker does not run on heat.

solution: A loudspeaker changes electrical energy into sound energy.

questions.stem: What is the main source of energy for living things on Earth?

explain.why: Soil gives plants minerals but not the energy they need to make food.
The Moon only reflects a little sunlight.
The wind itself gets its energy from the Sun.

solution: Plants use light from the Sun to make food, and animals eat plants or other animals.

questions.stem: Which of the following was formed from plants that lived long ago?

explain.why: Sunlight is light from the Sun, not a fuel formed from plants.
Flowing water is not formed from plants.
Wind is moving air. It is not formed from plants.

solution: Coal was made from the remains of plants that were buried for millions of years. These plants used energy from the Sun.

questions.stem: A windmill pumps water from a well. The energy of the wind comes from which source?

explain.why: Clouds do not give energy to the air.
The sea does not make the wind. The Sun heats air and water unevenly.
The Moon does not heat the air.

solution: The Sun heats the air unevenly, and the warm air rising makes the wind blow.

questions.stem: A rubber band is stretched and held. Which form of energy does it have?

explain.why: A rubber band held still makes no sound.
A rubber band does not give out light.
The rubber band is not moving while it is held.

solution: A stretched rubber band stores elastic potential energy.

questions.stem: Ali rolls the same ball at four different speeds. When does the ball have the most kinetic energy?
options: When it rolls at any speed

explain.why: The slower the ball, the less kinetic energy it has.
Kinetic energy gets bigger as the speed gets bigger.
A ball that has stopped has no kinetic energy.

solution: The faster an object moves, the more kinetic energy it has.

questions.stem: A ball is held at different heights above the floor. At which height does it have the most potential energy?

explain.why: 20 cm is the lowest, so it gives the least potential energy.
A greater height gives more potential energy, and 35 cm is not the highest.
A greater height gives more potential energy, and 50 cm is not the highest.

solution: The higher the ball, the more potential energy it has. The heights were 20 cm, 35 cm, 50 cm and 80 cm.

questions.stem: Which of these things has both kinetic energy and potential energy?
options: A candle that is not lit
A bird flying high in the sky
A parked car on level ground
A book lying on the floor

explain.why: It is not moving and not high up.
It is not moving and not high up.
It is neither moving nor high up.

solution: The bird is moving (kinetic energy) and high above the ground (potential energy).

questions.stem: In which of the following is electrical energy changed into light energy?
options: A solar panel on a calculator

explain.why: A solar panel changes light into electrical energy.
A doorbell changes electrical energy into sound energy.
A fan changes electrical energy into kinetic energy.

solution: A lamp changes electrical energy into light energy.

questions.stem: A ball is released at P and rolls down the track to Q. Which energy conversion mainly takes place?

explain.why: The ball is not heated. It speeds up because it goes lower.
That would happen if the ball went up the slope. It is going down.
The ball does not give out light.

solution: The ball goes lower, so it loses potential energy and gains kinetic energy.

questions.stem: A toy car is pushed and then rolls along the floor until it stops. Into which form of energy is its kinetic energy mainly changed?

explain.why: The toy car does not give out light.
No electricity is made as the car slows down.
The car did not go up, so it did not gain potential energy.

solution: Friction between the wheels and the floor changes the kinetic energy into heat energy.

questions.stem: Plants use energy from the Sun to make food. Which form of energy from the Sun do plants use?

explain.why: The Sun does not send sound to the Earth.
Plants do not use movement energy from the Sun.
The Sun does not give plants electrical energy.

solution: Leaves take in light energy from the Sun to make food.

questions.stem: Which two forms of energy does a burning candle give out?

explain.why: A candle flame is silent and does not move anything.
A candle flame is not an object that moves or is lifted.
A candle makes no electricity.

solution: The flame lights up the room and makes the air around it warm.

questions.stem: Wind turns the blades of the turbine, which turns the generator and lights the bulb. Which energy conversion takes place in the generator?

explain.why: The generator does not give out light. The bulb does.
The generator is turned by moving blades, not heated.
That is what a motor does. A generator makes electricity.

solution: The turning generator changes kinetic energy into electrical energy.

questions.stem: A pendulum bob swings from A to C and passes B, the lowest point. At which position does the bob have the most kinetic energy?

explain.why: The bob stops for a moment at A and at C, so it has the least kinetic energy there.
At C the bob is at its highest point and stops for a moment, so its kinetic energy is the least.
At A the bob is at its highest point and stops for a moment, so its kinetic energy is the least.

solution: The bob moves fastest at the lowest point B, so its kinetic energy is greatest there.

questions.stem: A pendulum bob swings from A down to B, the lowest point. What happens to its potential energy and kinetic energy?
options: Potential energy increases and kinetic energy decreases
Potential energy stays the same and kinetic energy increases
Potential energy decreases and kinetic energy increases
Both potential energy and kinetic energy increase

explain.why: Going down loses potential energy and the bob speeds up, so kinetic energy increases.
The bob is lower at B than at A, so its potential energy is less.
The bob is going lower, so its potential energy cannot increase.

solution: As the bob goes lower, potential energy changes into kinetic energy.

questions.stem: A pendulum swings a little lower each time and finally stops. What happens to its energy?
options: It is changed into light energy given out by the bob
It is changed into heat by friction at the hook and in the air
It is used up in each swing and disappears from the pendulum
It goes back into the string and is stored there as potential energy

explain.why: A pendulum does not give out light as it slows.
Energy does not disappear. It changes into other forms.
The string does not store the energy, and the bob does not rise again.

solution: Friction at the hook and the air rubbing against the bob change some energy into heat each swing.

questions.stem: A marble is released at P, rolls down to Q and up the other side to R. At which position does the marble have the most kinetic energy?
options: It is the same at P, Q and R

explain.why: The marble speeds up going down, so its kinetic energy changes.
At P the marble has only just been released, so its kinetic energy is the least.
At R the marble is higher and slower, so it has less kinetic energy than at Q.

solution: Q is the lowest point, where the marble moves fastest.

questions.stem: A marble is released at P, rolls down to Q and up the other side. It stops at R, which is lower than P. Why does the marble not reach the height of P?
options: Gravity pulls harder on the right-hand side
Its energy is changed into light energy
The marble gets lighter as it rolls
Some of its energy is changed to heat by friction

explain.why: Gravity pulls with the same force everywhere on the track.
A rolling marble does not give out light.
A marble does not lose matter as it rolls.

solution: Friction changes some of the marble's energy into heat, so it cannot climb as high as P.

questions.stem: A roller-coaster car is released at P. Which statement about the car moving from Q to R is correct?
options: Potential energy is changing into kinetic energy
Kinetic energy is changing into potential energy
The car gains both kinetic energy and potential energy
Kinetic energy is changing into sound energy only

explain.why: Going up a hill, the car slows down and gains height.
It slows down as it climbs, so its kinetic energy decreases.
Most of the change is into potential energy as the car climbs.

solution: From Q to R the car rises and slows down, so kinetic energy changes into potential energy.

questions.stem:
Which of the following statements about energy are correct?
A: A moving car has kinetic energy.
B: A stretched spring has potential energy.
C: A lit bulb has no energy.
D: Sound is not a form of energy.

explain.why: Both C and D are wrong.
A lit bulb gives out light energy and heat energy, so C is wrong.
Sound is a form of energy, so D is wrong.

solution: A and B are correct. A lit bulb gives out light and heat, and sound is a form of energy.

questions.stem: A cyclist pedals and the dynamo lights the lamp. What is the form of energy X in the energy chain shown?

explain.why: Heat is given out as well, but it is not what lights the lamp.
The dynamo does not turn the movement into sound.
The dynamo does not lift anything higher or store energy by height.

solution: The turning dynamo makes electrical energy, which the lamp changes into light.

questions.stem: A lift is raised by an electric motor. In the energy chain shown, which row gives X and Y?
options: X: electrical energy; Y: light energy
X: light energy; Y: kinetic energy
X: electrical energy; Y: kinetic energy
X: kinetic energy; Y: electrical energy

explain.why: The lift moves up, so it gains kinetic energy, not light.
A lift motor does not run on light.
A motor takes in electricity and gives out movement.

solution: A motor changes electrical energy into kinetic energy.

questions.stem: A wind-up toy car is wound up, put on the floor and let go. It moves forward. Which energy conversion mainly takes place?
options: Potential energy in the spring to kinetic energy
Kinetic energy to potential energy in the spring

explain.why: The toy does not use light.
A wind-up toy is not driven by heat.
Winding stores energy in the spring. Letting go gives it back as movement.

solution: Winding the spring stores potential energy, which changes to kinetic energy as it unwinds.

questions.stem: A toy car runs on a battery. While it moves, its lights shine and its horn sounds. Which forms of energy is the electrical energy changed into?

explain.why: The car moves, so kinetic energy must be included.
The horn gives out sound, so sound energy must be included.
The car does not store energy by going higher, so there is no potential energy.

solution: The motor gives kinetic energy, the lights give light and the horn gives sound.

questions.stem:
Which of the following change electrical energy into heat energy?
A: An electric iron
B: A radio
C: A rice cooker
D: A ceiling fan

explain.why: A fan changes electrical energy into movement.
A radio gives sound and a fan gives movement.
A radio changes electrical energy into sound.

solution: An electric iron and a rice cooker are heated by electricity.

questions.stem: The table shows the energy conversions in four devices. Which device is shown wrongly?

explain.why: A fan does change electrical energy into kinetic energy.
A radio does change electrical energy into sound energy.
A torch does change electrical energy into light energy.

solution: A solar cell changes light energy into electrical energy. The table shows it the wrong way round.

questions.stem: A book is lifted from the floor and put on a high shelf. Which statement about the book is correct?
options: Its kinetic energy has increased because it was moved
It has gained no energy because it is at rest
Its potential energy has increased because it is higher
Its potential energy has decreased because it is further from the floor

explain.why: On the shelf the book is at rest, so it has no kinetic energy.
Being high up gives it potential energy even when it is at rest.
The higher an object is, the more potential energy it has.

solution: Lifting the book needs energy, which is stored as gravitational potential energy.

questions.stem: Dina eats her breakfast and then runs. What happens to the energy stored in her food?
options: It is lost as sound when she breathes
It changes into kinetic energy and heat in her body
It changes into light energy in her muscles
It changes into electrical energy and stays in her muscles

explain.why: Only a tiny part of the energy leaves as sound.
Muscles do not give out light.
Her body does not store energy as electricity for running.

solution: The energy stored in food is used for movement (kinetic energy) and keeps the body warm (heat).

questions.stem: Which pair of devices shows the main energy conversions correctly?
options: Electric fan: electrical to kinetic; solar panel: electrical to light
Electric fan: electrical to kinetic; solar panel: light to electrical
Electric fan: electrical to heat; solar panel: heat to electrical
Electric fan: kinetic to electrical; solar panel: light to electrical

explain.why: A solar panel changes light into electricity.
A fan mainly makes movement, and a solar panel uses light.
A fan uses electricity to move. It does not make electricity.

solution: Both conversions in the correct row are right.

questions.stem: A filament bulb is hot after it has been switched on for a while. Why?
options: Some of the electrical energy is changed into heat energy
The bulb takes in heat energy from the room
All the light energy is changed into heat energy

explain.why: The heat comes from the bulb itself.
Nothing inside the bulb is moving to store kinetic energy.
Some energy still leaves as light, and the light comes from electrical energy.

solution: A bulb changes electrical energy into light and heat.

questions.stem: Water stored high behind a dam flows down to turn a turbine, which turns a generator. Which row shows the order of the energy conversions?
options: Kinetic energy, potential energy, electrical energy
Potential energy, kinetic energy, electrical energy
Potential energy, electrical energy, kinetic energy
Electrical energy, kinetic energy, potential energy

explain.why: The water is high first, so it has potential energy first.
The turbine moves before the generator makes electricity.
A generator makes electricity at the end of the chain.

solution: Water high up has potential energy, moving water has kinetic energy, and the generator makes electrical energy.

questions.stem: A diver jumps from the end of the bent springboard shown. As the board straightens and pushes the diver up, which energy conversion mainly takes place?
options: Heat energy of the board to kinetic energy of the diver
Elastic potential energy of the board to kinetic energy of the diver
Light energy to kinetic energy of the diver
Kinetic energy of the diver to elastic potential energy of the board

explain.why: The board is not hot. It is bent.
The diver does not use light energy to jump.
That happens when the diver lands on the board. Here the board is pushing the diver up.

solution: The bent board stores elastic potential energy, which becomes the diver's kinetic energy.

questions.stem: A ball is thrown straight up. At its highest point, which statement is correct?
options: Its kinetic energy and potential energy are both zero
Its kinetic energy is the least and its potential energy is the greatest
Its kinetic energy is the greatest and its potential energy is the least
Its kinetic energy and potential energy are both the greatest

explain.why: It is high up, so it has a lot of potential energy.
At the top the ball stops for a moment, so kinetic energy is the least.
It has stopped for a moment, so its kinetic energy is the least.

solution: At the top the ball is highest and momentarily at rest.

questions.stem: Which sequence best shows how the energy in petrol came from the Sun?
options: Sunlight, wind, rocks that melt underground, petrol
Sunlight, plants long ago, buried remains, petrol
Sunlight, the Moon, soil that is pressed, petrol
Sunlight, water in the sea, rain collected underground, petrol

explain.why: Petrol is not formed from the wind or from rocks warmed by the Sun.
The Moon and soil are not part of how petrol is formed.
Petrol is not made from rain.

solution: Plants and animals that lived long ago got their energy from the Sun. Their remains were buried and slowly changed into fuels.

questions.stem: Hana says that the energy in the food we eat comes from the Sun. Which statement supports her?
options: Animals take in energy straight from the soil they walk on
Food stores up heat that it takes in from the warm air
Plants use sunlight to make food, and we eat plants or animals that ate them
The Sun cooks the food and the heat stays stored in it

explain.why: Animals do not get their energy from soil.
Food does not take heat from the air.
That heat does not give the food its stored energy.

solution: The energy in food started as light energy from the Sun that plants used to make food.

questions.stem: In which of these is kinetic energy changed into sound energy?
options: A battery is put in a torch
A band is stretched and held
A bulb is lit by a battery

explain.why: A battery in a torch gives electrical energy.
A stretched band stores potential energy.
A bulb changes electrical energy into light.

solution: The moving hammer hits the nail, and some of its kinetic energy becomes sound.

questions.stem: A hand warmer is switched on and becomes warm. Which energy conversion takes place?

explain.why: The device makes heat from electricity.
The hand warmer is not powered by light.
Nothing in a hand warmer moves to make electricity.

solution: Electric current heats the warmer.

questions.stem: The graph shows the kinetic energy and potential energy of a ball falling from a high place. Between which times are the two energies equal?

explain.why: In this time potential energy is far bigger than kinetic energy.
In this time potential energy is still the bigger one.
In this time kinetic energy is already the bigger one.

solution: The two lines cross between 2 s and 3 s, where both energies are about 50 units.

questions.stem: The graph shows how far a rubber-band toy car moves for different numbers of windings. Which conclusion is correct?
options: Fewer windings make the car move further
The car moves 30 cm further for each extra winding
The number of windings does not affect how far the car moves
More windings make the car move further

explain.why: The bars rise as the number of windings increases.
30 cm is the extra distance for 5 more windings, not for one.
The distance changes with the number of windings.

solution: More windings store more elastic potential energy, so more kinetic energy and a longer run.

questions.stem: The graph shows the height reached by a pendulum bob on each swing. Which statement best explains the graph?
options: The bob changes some of its energy to light in each swing
Some of the energy is changed to heat in each swing
The bob gains energy from the air in each swing
The Earth pulls the bob less strongly in each swing

explain.why: A pendulum does not give out light.
If it gained energy it would swing higher.
Gravity stays the same throughout.

solution: Friction at the pivot and with the air changes some energy to heat, so the bob rises less each time.

questions.stem: Which row shows the order of the forms of energy in a solar-powered fan?

explain.why: The solar cell must first take in light from the Sun.
A fan is moved by electricity and does not make light.
The fan moves because of the electricity, so electricity comes before movement.

solution: The solar cell changes light to electrical energy and the motor changes it to kinetic energy.

questions.stem:
Which of the following statements about energy are correct?
A: A moving object has kinetic energy.
B: Energy can be changed from one form to another.
C: A lit bulb changes only electrical energy into light.
D: An object high up has potential energy.

explain.why: C is wrong because a bulb also gives out heat.
A bulb also gives out heat, so C is wrong.
C is wrong because a bulb also gives out heat.

solution: A, B and D are correct. A bulb changes electrical energy into both light and heat.

questions.stem: A girl jumps on a trampoline. When she is at the lowest point, the trampoline is stretched most. Which statement is correct at that moment?
options: The elastic potential energy of the trampoline is the greatest and her kinetic energy is zero
Both her kinetic energy and the elastic potential energy are zero
Her kinetic energy is the greatest and the elastic potential energy of the trampoline is zero
Her gravitational potential energy is the greatest

explain.why: The stretched trampoline stores a lot of elastic potential energy.
She has stopped for a moment at the lowest point, so her kinetic energy is zero.
She is at her lowest point, so her gravitational potential energy is the least.

solution: The trampoline is stretched most, and she is momentarily at rest.

questions.stem: A bungee jumper falls from a high platform until the cord stretches and pulls her back up. At the lowest point, which statement is correct?
options: The cord has the greatest elastic potential energy and she has no kinetic energy
She has the greatest kinetic energy and the cord has no elastic potential energy
The cord and she have no energy
She has the greatest gravitational potential energy

explain.why: She stops for a moment at the lowest point and the cord is most stretched.
The stretched cord stores a lot of elastic potential energy.
She is at her lowest point, so her gravitational potential energy is the least.

solution: At the lowest point she has stopped, the cord is stretched most, and her energy is now stored in the cord.

questions.stem: A kettle is switched on and the water gets hot. Dan says that the electrical energy is used up. Which statement is correct?
options: The electrical energy goes back into the socket
The electrical energy is changed to heat energy and not destroyed
The electrical energy is changed to light energy
The electrical energy is destroyed and the heat is new energy

explain.why: Energy does not flow back to the socket.
A kettle makes the water hot. It does not mainly give out light.
Energy is never destroyed. It changes form.

solution: Energy is not used up. It is changed from one form to another.

questions.stem: The brake discs of a car become very hot after the car has stopped suddenly. Which statement explains this?
options: The car's potential energy is changed into heat energy by gravity
The heat energy of the road is changed into kinetic energy
The kinetic energy of the car is changed into heat energy by friction
The car's sound energy is changed into heat energy

explain.why: The car stopped on level ground and did not go down.
The car loses kinetic energy as it stops.
The sound the brakes make is only a tiny part of the energy.

solution: The brake pads rub against the discs, so friction changes the car's kinetic energy into heat.

questions.stem: A roller-coaster car is released at P and moves along the track without much friction. Which statement about the car at R compared with at P is correct?
options: It has the same potential energy as at P
It has no kinetic energy because it is on top of a hill
It has more potential energy than at P because R is a hill
It has less potential energy than at P and some kinetic energy

explain.why: R is lower than P, so the potential energy is less.
It is lower than P, so some potential energy has changed into kinetic energy.
P is higher than R, so P has more potential energy.

solution: R is lower than P. Some potential energy has changed into kinetic energy, so the car is still moving.

questions.stem: A wind-up toy car runs for 10 s on a smooth floor and for 6 s on a carpet. Why does it stop sooner on the carpet?
options: The carpet changes the heat of the car into kinetic energy
More of its energy is changed to heat by friction on the carpet
The carpet gives the car less potential energy
The spring stores less energy when the car is on a carpet

explain.why: Friction changes kinetic energy into heat, not the other way round.
The carpet does not change how much energy is stored in the spring.
The spring stores the same energy. It is wound the same way.

solution: The carpet has more friction than the smooth floor.

questions.stem: Joel stretches a rubber band by different amounts and lets it go to shoot a paper ball. The ball goes further when the band is stretched more. Which statement explains this?
options: A band stretched more gives out more light energy when it is let go
A band stretched more becomes heavier, so it pushes the ball further
A band stretched more has more kinetic energy while it is held still
A band stretched more stores more elastic potential energy to give kinetic energy

explain.why: A rubber band does not give out light.
Stretching does not make the band heavier. It stores more energy.
A band that is held still has no kinetic energy.

solution: More stretch stores more elastic potential energy, so the ball gets more kinetic energy.

questions.stem: A solar-powered toy car works only when a bright lamp shines on its panel. Which statement is correct?
options: The motor changes light energy into electrical energy, which the panel changes into movement
The panel changes sound energy into electrical energy
The panel changes heat energy into kinetic energy, which the motor changes into light
The panel changes light energy into electrical energy, which the motor changes into kinetic energy

explain.why: The panel is the part that takes in the light.
The lamp gives light, not sound.
The panel needs light, and the motor does not give out light.

solution: The solar panel takes in light and makes electricity. The motor uses electricity to move the wheels.

questions.stem: What forms of energy are produced when a hammer hits a nail into wood?

explain.why: The nail is not lifted and no electricity is made.
A hammer and nail do not make light or electricity.
No electricity is made by a hammer.

solution: The impact makes a noise, and the nail and wood become slightly warm because of friction.

questions.stem: In a hydroelectric power station, which row shows what happens in the generator?
options: Potential energy of the water to kinetic energy of the turbine
Kinetic energy of the turbine to electrical energy
Electrical energy to heat energy in the water
Electrical energy to kinetic energy of the turbine

explain.why: This happens as the water falls and hits the turbine, before the generator.
The generator does not heat the water.
That would be a motor. A generator makes electricity.

solution: The turbine turns the generator, which changes kinetic energy into electrical energy.

questions.stem: A swing is pulled back to position A and let go. It swings to B, the lowest point, and then to C on the other side. At which positions is its potential energy the same?

explain.why: The potential energy at the lowest point B is less.
B is the lowest point, so its potential energy is the least.
C is higher than B, so the potential energy is more at C.

solution: A and C are at the same height, so they have the same potential energy.

questions.stem: A ball is dropped from a high place. Just before it hits the ground, which statement is correct?
options: Its potential energy is the same as at the start
Most of its potential energy has changed into kinetic energy
Most of its kinetic energy has changed into potential energy
All of its potential energy has changed into light energy

explain.why: It is lower now, so it has less potential energy.
As it falls, it loses height, so it loses potential energy.
A falling ball does not give out light.

solution: As the ball falls, potential energy changes to kinetic energy.

questions.stem: The graph shows how high a ball rises after each bounce. Which statement explains why the heights get smaller?
options: Some energy is changed to heat and sound at each bounce
The ball gets more potential energy at each bounce
The ball changes some of its energy to light at each bounce
The Earth pulls harder on the ball at each bounce

explain.why: If it gained energy it would rise higher.
A bouncing ball does not give out light.
Gravity stays the same.

solution: Each bounce changes some of the ball's energy into heat and sound, so less is left to raise it.

questions.stem: Which row shows the energy conversion that mainly takes place in a microphone and in a loudspeaker?
options: Microphone: sound to kinetic; loudspeaker: kinetic to heat
Microphone: sound to electrical; loudspeaker: electrical to sound
Microphone: light to sound; loudspeaker: electrical to light
Microphone: electrical to sound; loudspeaker: sound to electrical

explain.why: The main conversion in each is between sound and electrical energy.
A microphone does not use light.
The two are the wrong way round.

solution: A microphone turns sound into electrical signals, and a loudspeaker turns them back into sound.

questions.stem: Which of the following shows a change from kinetic energy to potential energy?
options: A boy kicks a ball straight up and it rises
A stretched spring pulls a toy car forward
A ball rolls down a slope

explain.why: That changes electrical energy into light.
That changes elastic potential energy into kinetic energy.
Rolling down changes potential energy into kinetic energy.

solution: As the ball rises it slows down but gains height.

questions.stem: Which sequence shows how energy from the Sun is used to make electricity in a hydroelectric power station?
options: The Sun's light is stored in the dam water, the water is released, it makes electricity by itself
The Sun heats the dam, the water boils, steam turns a turbine, electricity is made
The Sun heats sea water, rain falls on high ground, the water flows down and turns a turbine, electricity is made
The Sun makes the wind, the wind pushes the water up the dam, electricity is made

explain.why: Water does not store light. It needs a turbine and a generator.
A hydroelectric station uses falling water, not steam.
The wind does not push the dam water. Rain fills it.

solution: The Sun's heat makes water evaporate and fall as rain on high ground. The water has potential energy, and as it flows down it turns a turbine.

questions.stem: A roller-coaster car is released at P and rolls along the track without friction. At which position does the car have the most kinetic energy?
options: It is the same at P, Q and R

explain.why: R is higher than Q, so the car is slower there than at Q.
The speed of the car changes along the track, so its kinetic energy changes too.
The car starts at rest at P, so its kinetic energy is the least.

solution: Q is the lowest position, so the car has lost the most potential energy and moves fastest there.
